title: Quarterly priorities deconflict canvas and talk track
summary: Working draft to align exec talking points, conflict map between team OKRs, and a compact all-hands run-of-show. Focus is on reducing cross-team friction before the quarter starts and surfacing escalation paths.
content:
Purpose:
- Short doc for FYQ4 kickoff: align exec messaging, surface OKR overlaps, and create a clear set of operational asks for teams ahead of the all-hands. Not a final plan; this is the deconflict layer and talk track scaffold.

Context and constraints:
- Company focus: reduce inference unit cost by 20% while maintaining latency SLOs and shipping Redwood Optimize beta.
- Capacity: Dedicated capacity ramp is delayed by ~3 weeks from infra plan (risk to Dedicated onboarding OKR).
- Hiring: ML infra hiring slower than forecast -> potential feature gating for Q4 guardrails.

High-level asks for the all-hands (what execs should make visible):
1) Priorities in one line each (30s per exec):
   - CEO: North star and why cost/latency tradeoffs matter to roadmap.
   - CTO: Where serving-runtime investments land vs. product-facing work.
   - Head of Product: Customer use cases we must protect (hosted API reliability, Dedicated SLAs, Private pilot pipeline).
2) One explicit escalation rule: if a deadline shifts > 2 weeks, the owning PM must open a cross-functional decision triage and tag the exec rota.
3) Visible commitment: amount of cross-team capacity (FTE-weeks) reallocated to Optimize beta stabilization.

Deconflict canvas (current overlaps & proposed mitigations):
- Serving-runtime latency work vs. Optimize batching: both require kernel-level changes on the same infra nodes.
  Proposed: schedule kernel landing window first 2 weeks Q4, then Optimize microbench changes in weeks 3-6; create a shared QA harness.
- Dedicated onboarding vs. Private installs pilot: capacity for infra engineers limited.
  Proposed: freeze non-critical infra migrations; triage Private installs to partner engineers where possible; use canary on Dedicated instead of full rollout.
- Observability retention asks (Console) vs. storage budget: product wants 90-day traces, finance pushes back.
  Proposed: hybrid retention: 30-day full traces + 90-day aggregated metrics; show cost delta in all-hands.

Draft OKR snippets (input for team OKR pages) -- keep short, measurable, and conflict-aware:
- Objective: Deliver predictable inference economics for customers.
  - KR1: Reduce average hosted API p95 token cost by 20% vs baseline (measure: cost/token)
  - KR2: Maintain text-generation median latency <= 160ms for top 10% of routes
  - KR3: Successful public beta of Redwood Optimize with 5 pilot customers and documented cost wins
Notes: flag KR2 dependency on serving-runtime kernel changes (see deconflict canvas).

Run-of-show for a 60-minute all-hands (compact, keeps exec asks visible):
- 0:00–0:05 Welcome + single-sentence company focus (CEO)
- 0:05–0:15 Product + Tech alignment (CTO + Head of Product; 5 min each)
- 0:15–0:25 Operational commitments and timelines (Eng leads; short heatmap slide)
- 0:25–0:35 OKR snapshot and top 3 cross-team risks (Product-ops)
- 0:35–0:50 Panel Q&A with preseeded questions + live acceptance (moderator: People Ops)
- 0:50–0:60 Closing: explicit asks, escalation path, and 48-hour follow-up doc link

Preseeded Q&A (for panel prep)
- How will we measure "cost wins" for Optimize pilots? (Answer prep: pilot dashboard metrics + cost-per-token delta)
- What happens if Dedicated ramp slips past the quarter? (Answer prep: fallback to increased hosted capacity + customer communications timeline)
- Will privacy/regulatory requirements delay Private installs? (Answer prep: yes for some customers; surface priority customers and alternative compliance packaging)

Communication map and timeline (one week before -> two weeks after):
- D-7: Share one-pager to execs + ask leads to confirm readiness slides (owner: product-ops)
- D-3: Dry run with slide owners and tech leads; record common questions (owner: eng-comm)
- Day 0: All-hands broadcast + link to follow-up doc with explicit owners and deadlines (owner: CEO office)
- D+2: Publish decision log and rebaseline OKR dependencies (owner: product-ops)

Decision points for exec sync (items to triage during pre-all-hands exec meeting):
- Approve the kernel landing window and temporarily block unrelated infra changes during that window.
- Confirm the cross-team capacity allocation number for Optimize stabilization (FTE-weeks).
- Sign off on the fallback communications plan for Dedicated customers if ramp delays persist.

Risks and mitigations (short list):
- Risk: Two major infra changes collide -> mitigation: narrow kernel change scope and require feature flags.
- Risk: Customer-facing SLA regression during Dedicated backfill -> mitigation: pre-approved compensation framework and customer success playbook.
- Risk: Messaging confusion across org -> mitigation: single one-pager + talk-track bullets; make it required for all slide decks.

Ownership and immediate next steps (this week):
- Product-ops (Maya): finalize the one-pager and distribute to execs by D-7.
- Eng leads (Diego): confirm kernel window and list of blocked PRs.
- Observability (Sofia): produce cost delta slide for retention options.
- CS/Sales (Priya): prepare customer notification draft for Dedicated fallback.

Open questions for this doc (please add inline comments in Drive):
- Do we want a live demo of Optimize pilot at the all-hands or save it for a product webinar?
- Is the proposed hybrid retention acceptable for legal/compliance?

Appendix (helpful links and artifacts):
- Link to current OKR draft: confluence:company-okrs-q4-draft
- Kernel landing proposal: github:org/serving-runtime/pulls/182
- Dedicated ramp plan: confluence:dedi-ramp-plan-2024

Notes to self (rough checklist):
- Collect pilot results (numbers + customer quotes) by D-3
- Ensure slides have single-sentence takeaways on top
- Prepare an FAQ doc for managers to cascade down to ICs
